title: an ordinary object literal with a member named match is not the compiler's Result.match: it compiles and its own method runs
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx §4 (Locked) forbids invalidating TypeScript's own escape hatches, and `match` is an ordinary identifier a user may name a member. 01-result-lifting/result-match-requires-both-branches pins the compiler's `match`; this pins the boundary — the member NAME is not what makes a call the compiler's. MEASURED BEFORE THE ROUND-7 FIX: this program did not merely fail to compile, it CRASHED the reference frontend with `Debug Failure. type must be class or interface`, exit 2, from `checker.getBaseTypes` called on a type that is neither. The rule that routed into that walk was reached by member name, so every ordinary object with a `match` method took the compiler down; thirteen receiver kinds were measured crashing (object literal, `as const` object, type-alias-typed value, union of literals, cast through `unknown`, mapped `Record`, function with a property, `null` under a cast, a `Proxy` type, an instantiated type parameter, a `satisfies` wrapper, `Object.freeze`, and a getter), across all six call spellings. The Go fork ran all of them correctly, so this was a REFERENCE-ONLY defect the corpus could have seen as a divergence for as long as it existed — and did not, because no case named this program. THE THREE SPELLINGS ARE THE POINT OF THE LINE COUNT. Round 7 also taught the member-selection helper to resolve a const-aliased element-access key, so `own[KEY]()` now resolves to the same member symbol as `own.match()` and reaches the same rule; a fix keyed on `PropertyAccessExpression` would leave the third spelling to crash. Its siblings are 01-result-lifting/a-frozen-object-with-a-match-method-compiles (a synthesized, symbol-bearing, non-class object type) and 01-result-lifting/a-module-member-named-match-is-the-modules-own (a module namespace receiver). The rules that must still fire are pinned elsewhere and were measured unchanged: SMITHERS1251, 1253, 1254 and 1255 on a real Error `match`, and SMITHERS1103 on a non-Error throw, which is what 01-result-lifting/a-thrown-object-literal-is-not-a-recoverable-error pins.
